overview.headline: Balanced cruise and unbalanced forces that make aircraft climb, fall, speed or slow

keyPoints.point: studying simplified motion means treating aircraft forces as balanced separately to build insight
keyPoints.quote: By simplified motion we mean that some of the four forces acting on the aircraft are balanced by other forces

keyPoints.point: level cruise has weight balanced by lift while drag is balanced by thrust
keyPoints.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

keyPoints.point: acceleration of the aircraft follows from mass and net force acting on it
keyPoints.quote: Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

keyPoints.point: net force equals opposing forces difference such as lift minus weight and thrust minus drag
keyPoints.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

keyTerms.gloss: upward force that can be balanced by weight
keyTerms.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

keyTerms.gloss: downward pull balanced by lift in level flight
